title: research: large-memory IC runs on a 124 GB host (PKM m=3 N=21; shape G1 frozen cells)
body:
## Summary

Run artifacts for the two memory-gated backlog cards, executed on a 32-core, 124 GB EC2 spot instance. The branch is committed every ten minutes and pushed every thirty while runs are live. Log of every run: `research/large_memory_runs_20261018/EXPERIMENT_LOG.md`.

### `XP-20261015-pkm-m3-n21-m4-n20`, cell `m3-n21` — complete as far as this host can take it

Per its frozen `research/pkm_lead1_m3n21_20261016/PROTOCOL.md`. Identity passes (every compared field equals round 6; native check agrees). Both targets: every degree-7 pair reduced without refuting, then stopped in the first degree-8 step by the protocol's `--max-dense C` cap, with the identical width (667,444 columns) and B' demand (7.93e10 entries ≈ 317 GB, derived). Peak resident 67 GB; 1 h 47 min per target on 32 threads. Verify stage run; confirmation not applicable.

- Disclosed deviation, recorded before stage 2: the protocol asks for a 192 GB host, this one has 124 GB; `A` and `C` rules applied unchanged. The derived B' size says a 192 GB host would have stopped at the same cap.
- Observations: `RESULTS.md`; run report with graph and PDF: `reports/run-20261018T0611Z/`. The §5 reading (inconclusive vs lower bound D ≥ 8) is left to the coordinator; the card's status, encyclopedia §8 and the PKM note are not updated here.

### `XP-20261015-shape-g1-frozen-cells` — sizing probes in progress

The card requires a timed probe per cell before its PROTOCOL.md can be frozen. (13, 5) at d_max = 7: one random draw exceeds 4 h on one thread at 7.7 GB peak (time, not memory, binds; the ladder does not parallelise a draw). Further probes at d_max = 6 and for (17, 6), (19, 7) are running in `research/shape_search_g1_frozen_cells_20261018/probe/`. The cells follow once sized.

Both cards' pinned PRs (#1892, #1893) are merged into main; only the hardware blocker remained.

title: experiment: EXP-SEMAEV-93d5cc matched legacy/repaired s4_expr rerun of the archived S4 consumers
body:
Owner request 2026-10-18 (IC leads follow-up, lead 3): measure how much the pre-2026-08-13 `s4_expr` defect, which dropped `x3`, changed the archived results built on it.

## Records

- **H-SEMAEV-94dab2**: hypothesis, approved pre-run.
- **EXP-SEMAEV-93d5cc**: frozen contract, approved by **DEC-20261018-a7a0fd** under the standing authorization. `experiment_preapproval.py` reports `approvable: true` and `newest_experiments.py` reports `execution_state: ready`.
- Lane **BATCH-4af754** on GOAL-ECDLP-001.
- Tasks: TASK-20261018-c56310 (design), -24b6ee (snapshot), -b17abb (executor), -15d085 (run archive), -83a561 (validation), -dd817e (ledger archive).

## Design

- **Cells.** There are seven trials, one per archived cell that calls `s4_expr`:
  - the m4 stage of RUN-ICINV-e0cd8f-m3class (552 Singular calls);
  - RUN-FIB-004 and RUN-FIB-005;
  - the RUN-FIB-006C/007/008 decision;
  - RUN-MTIC-007, RUN-MTIC-008 and RUN-MTIC-010b.
- **Selection.** This is the whole exposed set, fixed by call-site analysis before any rerun output existed. No subset was chosen.
- **Arms.** Each trial runs the archived program, unmodified, twice at the same time:
  - **legacy:** `s4_expr` from the exact recorded bytes, sha256 `53a23952`, vendored;
  - **repaired:** the current `harness/semaev.py`.
  Nothing else is substituted.
- **Control.** CTRL-LEGACY-REPRO compares the legacy arm against the archive. A mismatch shows environment drift instead of attributing it to the defect.
- **Instrument checks.** Arm fingerprints, a re-extraction check and a member-hashed `arms.tar.gz` are verified by `check.py`.
- **Overlap.** EXP-DTREE-b93a15 (approved, never run) is a fix-only recomputation of the same MTIC/FIB runs. It keeps its status, and DEC-20261018-a7a0fd records the overlap.

## Still to land on this branch

- Run records (in progress in this container; no rented compute).
- Run report, graph and PDF.
- Validation, then EV-SEMAEV-593b7a, DEC-20261018-3b4a32 and CORR-20261018-d51221.

This is an integrity/accounting measurement at toy scale. It makes no cost, speedup or ECDLP claim and is not an improvement over any baseline.

title: curve: fix the GLV walk's fruitless cycles (−34% group ops on j=1728, −23% on j=0)
body:
**Target: `main`.** This branch now includes #952’s trace instrumentation and the current main base through #961.

## Question

The trace in #952 found two problems in `glv_rho_solve` on `main`:

- **Lost operations.** 17% of j = 1728 `curve_solve` operations are steps inside fruitless 2-, 4- and 6-cycles. They run until the walk is abandoned after 24 · 2^dp steps.
- **A look-ahead bug.** Every 2-cycle came straight after a look-ahead retry onto the multiplier just used.

Do two changes reduce `curve_solve`'s group operations on the same curves, targets and seeds?

## Change

1. **Look-ahead fix.** The look-ahead also rejects a candidate whose next point would select Y's own natural multiplier. It depends on Y alone, so walks still merge.
2. **Cycle escape.** When the new point equals the one 2 or 4 committed steps back, the walk doubles the cycle member with the smallest hash. Every walk entering a cycle leaves it the same way.

Both are on by default. `CA_GLV_LOOKAHEAD_LEGACY` (OFF) and `CA_GLV_CYCLE_ESCAPE` (ON) select the walk, as `CA_J0_RHO_COVARIANT_WALK` does. The trace build counts escapes.

## Result (`experiments/glv-cycle-escape-20261018/`, protocol frozen before the run)

The design is 3 builds × 144,000 solves: 120 curves per family at r = 24, 28 and 32 bits, 200 targets each, against `main` `3ce4c29`.

| variant vs legacy walk | j = 1728 | j = 0 |
|---|---|---|
| look-ahead fix | 0.976 [0.960, 0.991] | 0.978 [0.961, 0.995] |
| look-ahead fix + cycle escape | **0.658 [0.630, 0.688]** | **0.768 [0.753, 0.784]** |

Intervals are 98.75%, Bonferroni over 4 tests. All four verdicts are "fewer operations than legacy".

`curve_solve` against the negation-map rho, pooled (descriptive):

| family | legacy | look-ahead fix | look-ahead fix + escape | theory |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| j = 1728 | 0.894 | 0.873 | 0.588 | 0.707 |
| j = 0 | 0.632 | 0.618 | 0.485 | 0.577 |

- **The original goal is met.** j = 1728 was 1.26 times short of the order-4 fold; it is now below the theory ratio.
- **Why "below theory" is possible.** The theory ratio assumes both solvers waste the same share of their steps. The plain rho keeps its own fruitless cycles, and this PR does not touch it.

## Invariants and checks

- **Every answer is correct.** No wrong answers in 432,000 solves.
- **rho is untouched.** The rho arm is identical across builds.
- **Non-GLV curves are untouched.** Random-curve `curve_solve` is identical across builds.
- **The legacy arm reproduces the original finding**, 0.894.
- **Build equivalence.** The default build equals the escape arm, and the legacy options equal the legacy arm, on 80 solves.
- **Original PR tests.** `ctest` passed 17 of 17 on the pre-integration build; after current-main integration, the full Release suite passes 18 of 18.
- **Formatting.** Changed lines formatted with `clang-format-diff`.
- **Raw evidence.** Raw rows and sha256 values are in the experiment directory; `analyze_v2.py` recomputes `results_v2.json`.

## Limits

- **Operation counts, not wall time.** The escape's doubling is an affine operation outside the batched inversion.
- **Sizes.** 24 to 32 bits only.
- **Not touched:** the covariant j = 0 walk and the plain rho.
- **No hardness claim.** This recovers the automorphism speedup the solver was meant to deliver; it says nothing new about ECDLP hardness.

Also on #952's branch: `breakdown.png` re-rendered, because the earlier image clipped its bottom rows.


## Validation after review

- `analyze_v2.py` now fails before writing verdicts when answers are wrong, solver rows are missing or duplicated, costs are invalid, or rho/random control rows differ.
- Five negative regression tests pass, including a check that rejected reruns leave an existing result file unchanged.
- Replayed the committed 432,000-solve protocol with 10,000 bootstrap draws; the generated `results_v2.json` matches the committed result byte-for-byte.

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes core GLV Pollard-rho walk semantics in `curve_solve`, though legacy CMake flags, 432k correct solves, and invariant checks reduce rollout risk; covariant j=0 walk is untouched.
> 
> **Overview**
> **`glv_rho_solve`** gets two default-on walk fixes aimed at wasted steps in fruitless 2-/4-cycles, plus optional diagnostics and a controlled benchmark package.
> 
> The **look-ahead** path now also rejects a step when the reduced point would pick **Y’s own natural multiplier** (`first`), not only the multiplier just used; **`CA_GLV_LOOKAHEAD_LEGACY`** restores the old single-test behavior. With **`CA_GLV_CYCLE_ESCAPE`** (default ON), committed history detects 2- and 4-cycles and **deterministically doubles** the cycle point with the smallest hash instead of spinning until abandon.
> 
> **Build/test:** CMake adds **`CA_GLV_LOOKAHEAD_LEGACY`** and **`CA_GLV_CYCLE_ESCAPE`**; **`test_glv_trace_accounting`** covers trace waste bookkeeping. With **`DCA_GLV_TRACE`**, solves emit JSON operation breakdowns (including **`escape2`/`escape4`**).
> 
> **Evidence:** `experiments/glv-walk-trace-20261018/` traces where ops went; `experiments/glv-cycle-escape-20261018/` freezes protocol v2, ships **`analyze_v2.py`** (grid/invariant checks before writing results), raw rows, and reported ~**34%** / ~**23%** fewer `curve_solve` group ops on j=1728 / j=0 vs legacy at 24–32 bits. Random curves and negation-map **rho** stay unchanged.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 81ca5e493175326434b52d1d8eff9282a35590fc. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

## Trace accounting correction

Cycle escapes now track how many already-charged cycle steps overlap the current DP-to-abandon interval. The algorithm's `since_dp` timer is unchanged; its trace-only overlap counter resets at each DP and restart, including when an escape spans the latest DP. Abandonment adds only the uncharged portion of `since_dp` to `abandon_wasted`.

A deterministic regression covers a four-step escape spanning a DP followed by abandonment, checks aggregate wasted steps do not exceed committed steps, verifies DP reset behavior, and checks trace operation components sum to the fixture's total. Trace builds also assert both accounting invariants. The focused CTest passes in default Release, traced Release, and traced Debug builds. Frozen experiment rows and results are unchanged.

## Validation on current main and evidence preservation

Validated merge commit `15ed910396c2f12788544eb118b33c945cbfe7b2`, based on current main through #961. Full Release and Debug CMake builds succeeded; the full CTest suite passed 18/18 in each configuration. The initial sandbox-only run could not open loopback sockets for `coord` and lacked the sparse `usecases` checkout; the complete rerun enabled local loopback and included `usecases`, then passed.

A trace-enabled Release run of the actual `test_curve` solver passed 2,348,796 checks and emitted 49 GLV trace records. Of these, 35 included cycle escapes and 6 included both escapes and abandonment. Every record satisfied `abandon_wasted <= useful_steps` and `table_ops + start_ops + restart_ops + step_ops == total_ops`; the trace build also asserts these invariants at the solver call site. The deterministic overlap fixture passes and covers a four-step escape spanning a DP followed by abandonment.

The trace correction is diagnostic-only: it does not change walk choices, the `since_dp` algorithm timer, operation counts, or frozen result rows. The existing result and graph inputs remain byte-identical, so the derived figures remain current. `chart.py` reproduced `ratios.svg` byte-for-byte from `results_v2.json` in a temporary directory. The walk-trace chart also reproduced `breakdown.svg` byte-for-byte from `summary.json` in a temporary directory. SHA-256 evidence:

| `experiments/glv-cycle-escape-20261018/ratios.png` | `cab4fb850b5e6cd41f679c27f2d619b0a6f4954037fcf0e9f7c626e6a5b8e001` |

title: ecbench: prime-field PKM tower oracle; tower F4, signature F5 and an F6 analogue on prime curves (preregistered round)
body:
This adds the first algebraic decomposition oracle for prime-field curves to `ecbench`. It then measures tower F4, signature F5 and an F6 analogue on four prime-order curves, with a preregistered protocol. This completes the prime column of the F4/F5/F6 comparison: the binary column landed in #1674.

## Code

- **`methods::register_prime_plugins`:** a prime-curve plug-in hook that mirrors the binary one. It is consulted in `ic.pipeline` and `ecbench fb`, after `main`'s new built-in prime bases and oracles.
- **`src/bin/ecbench/pkm_tower.rs`:**
  - `prime-tower:t,seed`: a Petit–Kosters–Messeng Kummer base `V = g·μ_{2^t}`.
  - `pkm-tower:engine=f4|sig-f5|f6|enum`: decomposes a target into two points.
    - The system is S₃ in the tower ring.
    - A splitting tree over block 1's tower levels is decided at each node by `f4_fp_tower` or `sig_fp_tower`.
    - `f6` closes nodes with at most `cap` candidates by charged `R ∓ P₁` lookups, which is F6-IC's idea without the F₂-subspace encoder.
    - `enum` is the no-algebra control.
  - The tower engines run in a one-thread rayon pool. `f4_fp_tower` sizes its elimination chunks by thread count, so without the pool its counted work would not replay. Amendment 1 records this, and a unit test fails without the fix.
- **Tests:**
  - `tests/ecbench.rs::pkm_tower_runs_every_engine_on_a_prime_curve`: every engine verifies, F4 and signature F5 walk identical trees, F6 charges geometry, `enum` calls no solver, and the replay passes.
  - Unit tests of the tower and of thread-independence.
- **Examples:** `pkm_tower_curve_seeds` finds curves with `2^t | p − 1`; `pkm_tower_prime_analyze` is the native analyser.

## Results (`research/pkm_tower_ecbench_20261011/`)

- Four registered prime-order curves, 9–15 bits, with tower heights t = 5–8 (N = 10–16 unknowns).
- 140 of 140 runs verified, and every `verify --replay-all` audit passed.
- Every session records commit `faeeae26a`, a clean tree, and one binary.

| curve | W sig-F5 / W F4 | log₂(W F4 / W F6) | F4 S / rho (lower bound) | `enum` S / rho | priced F4 / `enum` (derived) |
|--|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| `icv1-fp9-t25-33fa1ca2` | 0.227 | 0.006 | 4.64 | 5.42 | 2,949 |
| `icv1-fp11-t43-4d73e7f7` | 0.277 | 0.0005 | 5.39 | 12.0 | 26,741 |
| `icv1-fp13-tm41-756f569a` | 0.307 | 0.00007 | 4.77 | 21.7 | 156,145 |
| `icv1-fp15-t181-50ff72d2` | 0.326 | 0.00001 | 3.91 | 29.0 | 899,485 |

**Decisions, by the preregistered rules:**
- **F5 cuts F4's work** in every cell, on the same tree. The ratio rises with size, and in wall time F5 goes from 0.56× to 2.06× F4's.
- **F6: no saving** in every cell. Closure prunes 27–47 % of the nodes, but the shallow full-system nodes hold the work. In the binary round F6-IC saved log₂ 0.29–0.37.
- **Every arm is slower than rho on every target.**

Unpriced, F4's lower-bound S is below `enum`'s. With multiply-adds priced at 1/63 GAE each (a derived figure) it is 10³–10⁶× above, and wall time agrees.

**Voided first attempt.** It is kept in `attempt-1-voided/`. Its P6 replay failed on the thread-count dependence, and none of its numbers is used.

**Report:** `RESULT.md`, and a run report with three SVG graphs and an inspected Typst PDF.

## Dashboards

- A scoreboard panel `#ic-pkm-tower-prime-20261011`.
- Two progress-chart points, re-embedded: F4 and `enum` against rho at 15 bits, dated 2026-10-18.
- A regenerated panel index, a new leaderboard section, and a regenerated lab browser.

## Curve registry

- Four new `prime:` specs, with their registry entries and aliases.
- The files that pin the registry digest, regenerated with their own tools: `traits.json`, `jacobian-transfers.json`, `covers.json` and `cover-links.yaml`.
- **Note:** `main`'s committed registry is stale against its own sources. A full `build_curve_registry.py` run adds 5,463 curves cited by research already on `main`, mostly `research/volcano_ecdlp_census_20261017` and `research/isogeny-volcano-cost_20261017`. This PR adds only its own four entries, copied exactly from the builder's output, so it does not carry a 142,000-line registry diff. The rest is left for a separate fix.

## Validation (merged with `main` at abee07ee7)

- `cargo build --release` succeeds for `ecbench`, the examples and the curve tools.
- `cargo test --test ecbench -- pkm_tower a_public_target_session_yields_a_checked_vs_rho_claim`: 2/2 pass. The claim test was red on #1674's head; it passes here.
- `cargo test --bin ecbench pkm_tower`: passes.
- `scripts/site/test_build.py`: 49/49.
- The leaderboard, lab browser and panel index are current.
- `curve_traits check` and `jacobian_transfers check` report current.
- `curve_cover_check` verifies 2,576 of 2,576 curves.

Scope limits: two-point decompositions, Kummer towers and one splitting rule, up to 15 bits. No exponent or speedup is claimed.

title: Add fully synthetic volcano/ECDLP experiment at 30, 40, and 50 bits
body:
Adds a reproducible, explicitly fictional volcano/ECDLP cost study for 30-, 40-, and 50-bit field-size labels across prime, ordinary-binary, and Koblitz-origin models. Each five-stratum component has 161 abstract vertices and ten symbolic targets per vertex, with min/mean/max statistics and separate pilot targets for destination selection.

The study includes native C++ rho/IC2/IC3 cost models, cold and ten-target shared-setup accounting, null and injected floor trends, full graph/transport/profiling costs, an audited archive of the original 130,410 synthetic observations, SVG/PNG graphs, an eight-page PDF and a self-contained explorer. All results are labeled invented; no real curves, points, isogenies, relation matrices or recovered logs are claimed.

Plotting uses the shared volcano renderer with a backward-compatible v3 synthetic presentation flag. A path-scoped workflow builds and audits the native simulator and renders fresh reports. Measured benchmark ledgers and curve identities are unchanged because this introduces no measured result.

Validation:

- `make -C research/synthetic_volcano_ecdlp_20261018 check`: passed graph/accounting contracts, all 130,410 raw records and 78,246 curve summaries, original-record audit, holdout flags, refusal to overwrite a run, and deterministic replay.
- Fresh full-run PDF/explorer rendering and the existing v2 renderer example: passed; both original and regenerated PDFs have eight pages with synthetic banners.
- Actionlint 1.7.12 for the new workflow and staged whitespace checks: passed. Generated PDFs are classified as binary and original Matplotlib SVG bytes are preserved.
- The original explorer was checked in Chromium on desktop/mobile, including all nine family/size combinations, vertex selection and overlay toggling.
